source.title: Bad Global Minima Exist and SGD Can Reach Them
source.authors: Sheng-Chao Liu; Dimitris Papailiopoulos; D. Achlioptas

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures training accuracy while varying initialization and training heuristics, bearing on whether SGD reaches near-zero training error under different conditions.
record.gate_note: The study reports that vanilla SGD reaches 100% training accuracy on true labels from random initialization across tested models and datasets, and also after random-label pretraining for nearly all settings. DenseNet is an explicitly noted exception on some datasets. Test-accuracy, distance, norm and robustness results do not measure the training-error behavior named by the versions and are omitted.
record.test_reason: The study directly measures training classification accuracy of large convolutional networks trained with SGD, including CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, using the same basic method and measure as V1's original evidence.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that random-label pretraining can lead vanilla SGD to perfectly fitting but poorly generalizing models, while regularization, data augmentation and momentum can overcome this initialization's generalization damage.
record.recipe_differences: Studies SGD under random or adversarial initialization, with and without data augmentation, L2 regularization and momentum; it does not test the claim's central comparison as a reproduction of another listed source.
record.method_sensitivity: Training accuracy is near 100% across initialization and heuristic choices; DenseNet is slightly below 100% on some datasets, and some CIFAR10 ResNet18 table entries are marginally below 100%.

fits_no_version.finding: Models with perfect true-label training accuracy can differ by up to 40 percentage points in test accuracy after random-label pretraining; training heuristics largely remove the generalization damage.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SGD's generalization depends on initialization and training heuristics even when training classification error is essentially zero.

record.problems: Reported aggregate training-accuracy curves are not accompanied by exact values for each model and dataset in the text; DenseNet exceptions are not specified by dataset or number. Table 2 reports five-run means with variation for ResNet18 on CIFAR10.
record.rows_left_out: Test accuracy, parameter distance, norm and adversarial-robustness results were omitted because they do not measure training classification error named by the versions. Figure-only training curves were not transcribed into individual model-by-dataset rows; the paper's text reports the relevant aggregate findings.

untested.parts: No systematic model-size comparison, early-stopping comparison, Adam experiments, or demonstration of regularized recipes leaving substantial training error. Random-label pretraining outcomes are described without complete per-model fitting accuracies.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student width comparison or measurement of spurious-local-minimum frequency.
No controlled depth comparison of plain and residual networks, or tests of the specified initialization exceptions.
No activation-matched initialization, signal-propagation, orthogonality, or trainable-depth comparison. Random versus adversarial initialization does not test these mechanisms.
No stability-threshold, curvature, catapult, or edge-of-stability measurements.
No controlled batch-normalization comparison or Fixup experiment.

missing.what: Random-label fitting outcomes during adversarial-initializer construction. Record the reported successful full fitting separately from architectures stopped at convergence below 100%; do not treat Algorithm 1's stopping target as a measured success for every architecture.
missing.locator: Section 2, Algorithm 1 and footnote 4; Section 3.3, random-label fitting discussion; Section 3.4, replication-factor discussion

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source listed for V1. Tiny departures from exactly 100% accuracy do not limit a claim allowing near-zero error. The unspecified DenseNet shortfalls do not establish substantial training error or justify a challenges verdict. The supplied text contains no readable numerical plot traces, so exact DenseNet errors cannot be recovered.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare model sizes, early stopping, Adam, or a broader range of regularized recipes for training error. Random-label fitting is part of adversarial initialization, but the reported accuracy results primarily concern subsequent training on true labels.
